Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Cucumber (Card Game) - Quick Rules 1.1 Overview 1.2 Gameplay 1.3 Round End & Scoring 1.4 Special Rules Cucumber (Card Game) - Quick Rules Overview Players: 2 or more. Deck: Standard 52-card deck (no Jokers). Card Rank: Ace (high), King, Queen, Jack, 10 down to 2 (low). Objective: Do not win the very last trick of a round. Gameplay Each player is dealt seven cards (fewer if more than seven players are participating). Play proceeds clockwise. Playing a Trick: The lead player plays any card face up. Following Play: Subsequent players must either: Play a card of equal or higher value than the current highest card in the trick (suit does not matter). Or, if they cannot or do not want to beat the high card, they must play their lowest card in hand. Winning a Trick: The player who played the highest card wins the trick and leads the next one. Ties: If there is a tie for the highest card, the person who played the card last wins the trick. Round End & Scoring The first six tricks are used to manage your hand for the final seventh trick. The player who wins the last (seventh) trick scores penalty points. Penalty points equal the value of the winning card (Ace = 14, King = 13, Queen = 12, Jack = 11, numeric cards at face value). Players are eliminated ("become a cucumber") once their total score exceeds 30 points . Special Rules If a player leads with an Ace, every other player must play their lowest card regardless of their hand's power. From Dave Parlett's The Penguin Book of Card Games:

Called Gurka in Swedish and Ogórek in Polish, this Baltic gambling game may be played for either money or for a simple point-score.

Each player is dealt six cards, ranking upwards 23456789TJQKA. The aim is to avoid taking the last trick.

Each trick is led by the winner of the previous trick (the first trick is led by the player to the dealer's left). Each in turn must then play a card equal to or higher in rank than the previous card played. If they cannot, they then must play their lowest card. Whoever plays the highest card, or the last played if equally high, wins the trick.

Whoever wins the last trick scores penalty points equal to the face value of the card they won the trick with (as does anyone who played a card of the same rank), counting Ace 14, King 13, Queen 12, and Jack 11.

A player reaching 30 points is a "cucumber" and drops out of the game.

[Rating: 6.5/10] First impressions: I thought this was a fun and fairly simple trick taking game that worked well with my kids. You are dealt a hand of 6 cards. On each trick you have to play a card that is equal to or higher than the card led, or your lowest card if you can't. Suits don't matter and there isn't a trump. The only trick that scores is the last one, which you don't want to win as it only scores negative points. So you are trying to keep your lowest card possible for the last trick so you don't win it.
